questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The quality and reputation of University of Edinburgh was a significant factor for choosing that destination for my exchange. Moreover, I did consider the economic benefits of being able to receiving Erasmus scholarship while being abroad, as well as the fact that english was the main language being taught and spoken there. Finally, I really appreciated the culture and nature Scotland offered.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My study abroad experience did live of to most of my expectations. Scotland (and Edinburgh specifically) is an amazing destination for exchange students, since it is a very international hub for many travellers and nomads.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy. I received a lot of information from my University. A bit overwhelming actually considering the amount of emails and links they sent me.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got quick responses from my contact persons.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Keep your hair on! It seemed impossible in the beginning to find student housing (I got my offer 2 weeks before my departure) , but when I arrived there were plenty of rooms still available. Be aware that you can often change student housing after arrival - so wait unpacking if this is something you want to try and apply for within the first weeks.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I actually enjoyed staying a bit outside of centrum. It gave me a more authentic experience of where people live, and was a key factor in terms of developing a strong bond with the people I lived with, since we often had social thing at my dorm.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Be aware that living a bit outside of the city center (off campus), does imply buying a bicycle or a buss pass - extra costs.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Just follow guidelines

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I just followed the guidelines provided in the emails I received.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email correspondences with KU and EU

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I applied for. It was difficult - and a bit frustrating - to get classes outside my programme, because I was on a special exchange agreement (Psychology). They were pretty strict about me not taking classes outside of the agreement, and not very flexible even thought I had mandatory courses I needed to find.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read your emails and act when they tell you to. Reach out to either KU or EU if you have any questions, they will help you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was satisfied with 2/3 of my courses. I was surprised however of the amount of self-study and read-load compared to classes. This is personally not something I prefer over seminars and in class discussions.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 3d year courses (meaning people were in the end of their bachelor programme). This was great, since people were not totally new in Uni, which was nice because a lot of the first years are also very young and inexperienced.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I was surprised however of the amount of self-study and read-load compared to classes. This is personally not something I prefer over seminars and in class discussions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Science of Close Relationships (PSYL101412025-6SV1),

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Science of Close Relationships (PSYL101412025-6SV1) and
Natural Language Processing for Psychologists (PSYL101862025-6SV1) were great.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Buss pass and also I had to buy ALL the things I needen in my dorms (from pillows, duvets, sheets and a bin to cutlery, pots, pans and knives). This cost my more than 1000dkk alone. Also, I spent a lot of money just exploring the city (going out for dinner, lunch and coffee) which is expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: More.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: EU have a LOT of societies - every hobby you can think of. Very active communities if you want to priorities that, and a good way to meet "locals".

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything - sports, book-clubs, soup-society, hot-chocolate society, politics, journalism, riding, sailing, hiking, art, debates, social voulenteering and many more.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I was part of the hill walking, but never got to attend any of their trips. I do think however it would have been fun. Also the yoga society of you are in to that.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the highlands (Inverness is a good destination to base yourself)!. Isle of Skye was amazing. I went with Erasmus and met a lot of nice people there, though the trip itself was a bit rushed.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. The scots look a lot like us danes.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join societies or take part in the student accommodation events - I met most of my friends through that (most international students though).

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The university social scene was a lot different than in Copenhagen. A lot of the social groups people engage in are through societies, which if you come from a danish background where you get a class you enrole in through your bachelor programme can come across as a bit odd.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The oppeness of the Scottish when travelling around and the love they have for their country. Also, the pub culture - very unique and diverse way of socialising and drinking compared to Danish bar culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Prepare which courses you want to take in advance. This is a major help in order to not be surprised by the rigidity of the process. You may change courses within the first 2 weeks so there is space for testing out something if you'd like. Also, engage in the social events in the beginning of the semester. Most people meet their groups in the beginning.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are younger than 22 you can apply for a young scots card which gives you discounts on busses. Also try the African wrap in front of Appleton Tower...

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met, and the connection I now have to Scotland and now Edinburgh. Also the improved academic confidence I've gained since studying in another language on my own in a whole new academic system.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Understanding the guidelines and requirements in the assessments were a bit challenging since it was so different from the KU standards, and also not having anyone to consult with (a study group) on different tasks. Some of the final assessments were pretty challenging, others were easier than in Denmark.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
